result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more processes touching the same resource, so the code works most of the time and fails occasionally. With a shared log, the danger is two scripts writing at once and their output interleaving mid-line, or one clobbering the other.

Always open the log with `>>` (never `>`), and take a lock around the write with `flock`:

```sh
{
  flock 9
  echo "$(date -Is) job started"
  echo "$(date -Is) details: $details"
} 9>>/var/log/app.log
```

`>>` opens the file in append mode, so each write lands at the current end of file even if another process has written in between. `flock` then makes the whole block exclusive, so multi-line entries stay together; the lock is released when the block ends and the descriptor closes.

For a single short `echo` line on a local filesystem, `>>` alone is enough in practice. The lock is unreliable on NFS, and every writer has to use it for it to protect anything.
